mainEntity.name: How can I make an AI webinar presentation accessible to people with disabilities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Design accessibility into the deck, platform settings, registration process, and follow-up materials from the beginning. Use readable contrast and text, meaningful slide titles, captions or a transcript, verbal descriptions of important visuals, and a low-bandwidth alternative when practical. Context: Accessibility guidance recommends treating inclusion as a core requirement and retaining manual or human support when automated tools fail. Key factors: - Caption accuracy and correction process - Screen-reader reading order - Visual and audio dependence - Participant accommodation requests Practical guidance: Test captions with domain-specific terms such as AI product names and prompts. Provide materials in an accessible format and tell attendees how to request support. Treat automated captions as a draft requiring review, especially when technical vocabulary affects meaning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan accessibility from the start: use readable slides, meaningful titles, strong contrast, captions, a reviewed transcript, verbal descriptions of key visuals, and accessible follow-up materials. Test technical terms in captions, offer a low-bandwidth option when practical, and provide a clear way to request support.
